transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... I mean, ever since I tried to turn my art into a real freelance business, things have just gotten so out of hand. I keep getting really wound up over invoices and client messages. It's funny, actually, because I used to love painting. I had this little studio set up in the corner of my living room by the window—it gets the best morning light, you know? My cat, Barnaby, always sleeps right in the sunbeam while I work. He's a tabby, very affectionate but totally demanding when it comes to breakfast. Anyway, where was I? Oh, right. So, I get so overwhelmed by the business side of it that I just avoid looking at my emails or messages until I'm literally sitting at my kitchen table crying. And then I end up forgetting normal stuff, like paying my own bills, because I'm so stressed about the art stuff. I don't know, I just thought making money doing what I love would be... better?
Do you find that you worry excessively about other things in your life, not just work-related issues, like everyday responsibilities or events, even when there isn't a clear problem to solve?

Um, no, not really. It's just the business stuff, mostly. Like, I don't sit around worrying about... I don't know, my health or the news or whatever. Speaking of the news, did you see that thing about the local farmers market? They're moving it to the park downtown, which is so annoying because parking there is a nightmare. I used to go every Sunday to get these specific heirloom tomatoes. The guy who sells them, Frank, he always saves me a basket because he knows I use them for this pasta sauce my grandmother taught me how to make. It takes like four hours to simmer, but it makes the whole apartment smell amazing. Barnaby always tries to jump on the counter when I'm cooking it, which is so bad, I know. But yeah, no, I don't think I worry about everything else. Just the art business stuff. It's just... it's all so much.
When you get worked up about the business stuff, do you notice any physical symptoms, like feeling restless, having trouble relaxing, or maybe muscle tension?

Physical symptoms? Um... I don't really think so. I don't feel restless or tense or anything like that. I just get really overwhelmed and start crying, like I said. But I don't feel it in my body, really. I mean, maybe I'm a little tired, but that's probably because I stay up so late trying to figure out how to format these invoice templates. Have you ever tried to use those online accounting programs? They are so confusing. They use all this jargon that I don't understand, and the customer service chat bots are completely useless. I spent an hour trying to get a real person on the line the other day, and they just kept sending me links to their FAQ page. It's like, if the FAQ page answered my question, I wouldn't be calling you, you know? And the hold music was this awful smooth jazz loop that kept cutting out. It reminded me of the music they play at the dentist's office. I actually need to go to the dentist soon, I think I have a cavity on my back molar. It twinges every time I drink iced coffee, which is a tragedy because I basically survive on iced coffee. But anyway... no, I don't really have any muscle tension or anything. Just the crying.
Have you noticed feeling down, depressed, or losing interest in activities you used to enjoy, like painting or cooking your grandmother's pasta sauce?

Feeling down? I mean, I guess I get upset about the emails and the invoices, but I wouldn't say I'm depressed. And I definitely haven't lost interest in painting! I still love it. It's just the business part that ruins it. Like, yesterday I was mixing this perfect shade of cerulean blue for a new piece. It took me forever to get it right because I was trying to match the color of this vintage glass vase I found at a flea market last summer. Oh my gosh, that flea market was amazing. It was out in the country, and they had all these old farm tools and antique furniture. I bought this beautiful wooden chair that needs a little refinishing, but I haven't gotten around to it yet because I've been so busy stressing over my art shop. I keep telling myself I'll sand it down on the weekend, but then the weekend comes and I just want to sit on the couch with Barnaby and watch those home renovation shows. Have you seen the one where they restore old Victorian houses? They always find the craziest things hidden in the walls, like old newspapers from the 1800s or weird little dolls. It's fascinating. But yeah, no, I still enjoy painting and cooking and stuff. I just hate the business side of it.
Have you felt down or had a low mood most of the day, nearly every day, even before the business stress started getting to you?

No, definitely not. I mean, before I started trying to sell my art online, I was totally fine. I was just painting and hanging out. I never really felt down like that every day. Actually, before I started the shop, I was spending a lot of time trying to train Barnaby to walk on a leash. Have you ever tried to put a harness on a cat? It is a production. He just flops over on his side and refuses to move, like his legs suddenly stopped working. It's hilarious, but also kind of frustrating because I bought this really cute little red harness that matches his collar. I thought it would be nice to take him to the park, you know? Get him some fresh air. But he just wants to sit on the balcony and watch the pigeons. There's this one pigeon that comes by every morning, and it has a little white patch on its wing. Barnaby just chatters at it through the screen door. It's so cute. But yeah, no, I didn't feel depressed or anything before all this business stuff started. I was just doing my normal thing.
When you're stressed about the business, do you find it hard to focus or make decisions, even about things you normally wouldn't have trouble with?

Hard to focus? Um, no, not really. I mean, I can still make decisions perfectly fine. Like yesterday, I had to decide what kind of wet food to get Barnaby because the brand I usually buy completely changed their recipe. Can you believe they do that without putting a huge warning on the label? I just happened to notice the pate looked a little more... yellow than usual when I opened a can. So I spent like twenty minutes in the pet aisle reading the tiny print on the ingredients. It turns out they added peas. Cats don't need peas! They're obligate carnivores. I ended up watching this whole documentary on YouTube about pet food manufacturing a few months ago, and it's actually really wild how much corn and filler they put into kibble. 

Anyway, I ended up just buying the chicken and liver one instead of the salmon. He seemed to like it fine. He ate the whole bowl and then immediately fell asleep in my laundry basket. I really need to fold those towels, actually. They've been sitting there since Tuesday, but they're so warm when they come out of the dryer, I feel bad moving him. But yeah, making decisions is fine for me. I don't lose focus or anything like that, just the crying about the business stuff.
Do you ever feel like your worrying about the business stuff is uncontrollable or goes on longer than you'd like, even if you try to stop thinking about it?

Uncontrollable worrying? No, I wouldn't say it's uncontrollable. I mean, I think about the shop a lot, sure, but I can definitely stop when I want to. Like, if I decide to go make a cup of tea, I just go make tea. Actually, I recently started ordering these loose-leaf teas from this little farm in Oregon. They have this one blend that's chamomile and lavender with just a tiny hint of peppermint. It is so soothing. I bought this beautiful glass teapot with a built-in infuser just for it, because the little metal tea balls always let the leaves escape into the water. Have you ever tried to drink tea and you get a mouthful of leaves? It completely ruins the experience. It feels like you're drinking swamp water. Anyway, I found the teapot at this thrift store downtown. The same thrift store where I got that vintage vase I was telling you about! They always have the best glassware. I think people just donate their grandmothers' old china cabinets without even looking at what's inside. I saw a complete set of depression glass there once, the really pretty green kind that glows under a blacklight. I almost bought it, but I don't really have the shelf space right now. But yeah, no, the worrying isn't uncontrollable. I just think about the business when I have to deal with it, you know?
Has this anxiety about your art business affected your ability to function in other important areas of your life, like your relationships, daily responsibilities, or overall quality of life?

Yeah, I guess it kind of has. I've been slipping up a little bit with my other freelance work and just normal home stuff. Like, I completely put off replying to this one freelance client for days because I was so hyper-focused on trying to keep up with my art display and getting everything to look perfect for the shop. He wanted me to design a logo for his dog-walking business, but he wanted the dog to look like a specific mix between a poodle and a pug. I think it's called a pugapoo? Or a poog? They look a little like fuzzy gremlins. They are absolutely adorable, but they're surprisingly hard to draw as a minimalist vector graphic. I spent hours just trying to get the curl of the tail right. 

And then, because I was so distracted by the art display, I actually missed my electric payment last week. Which is ridiculous because I desperately need the electricity to take photos of my paintings! I just bought these special daylight LED bulbs for my lamps. They're 5000 Kelvin, which is supposed to mimic natural noon sunlight. If you use regular soft white bulbs, all the paint colors look super yellow on camera, and then you have to spend forever in Photoshop color-correcting. I honestly hate color-correcting. It makes my eyes cross after a while. Do you ever get that thing where you stare at a screen too long and everything gets kind of fuzzy around the edges? I probably need to buy some of those blue light glasses. I saw a really cute tortoiseshell pair online the other day that would match my favorite cardigan... but anyway, yeah, I guess I've been dropping the ball a little on paying bills and emailing people back.
Do you feel that your anxiety about the business has caused you significant distress or made it hard for you to function in your work or at home?

Yeah, I mean, like I was just saying, it definitely has. It's been causing me a lot of stress, and it's making it hard to keep up with everything else. Like putting off that freelance client with the pugapoo logo, and missing my electric bill because I was so hyper-focused on getting the art display ready for the shop. 

Speaking of the electric bill, I actually had to call the company to get the late fee waived, and the woman on the phone had the most beautiful accent. I think she said she was from somewhere in Louisiana? It sounded so musical. I've always wanted to go to New Orleans. I saw this travel vlog where they went to this famous cafe and had beignets, and they were just covered in a mountain of powdered sugar. I don't know how you eat something like that without getting it all over your clothes. I'd probably have to wear a giant bib, like when you eat lobster. Have you ever had lobster? I tried it once at a wedding, but I think it was overcooked because it was really chewy. The wedding itself was beautiful, though—they got married in this botanical garden, and the hydrangeas were just massive. 

But yeah, the business stuff has definitely been making it hard to keep up with my freelance work and paying bills on time. It's just a lot to juggle right now.
Do you find that your worry about the business happens more days than not, and have you felt this way for at least several months?

More days than not? Um, no, I wouldn't say that. It's really just when I have to deal with the shop directly, you know? Like, it hasn't been several months of this constant worrying. It's just recent, since the shop stuff started piling up. 

Actually, speaking of time, I just bought this amazing vintage wall clock for my kitchen. It's one of those retro sunburst ones from the 60s? The spikes are made of this really cool brass that has a nice patina on it. I found it at an estate sale. Estate sales are so wild, you literally just walk through someone's entire life. I found a whole box of old postcards at that same sale, all addressed to this woman named Eleanor in the 1940s. The handwriting was gorgeous—that really swoopy, perfect cursive that nobody learns anymore. I tried to learn calligraphy once, but I am left-handed, so I just ended up smearing the ink everywhere. I had black ink on the side of my hand for like three days. It looked like a terrible bruise. My mom thought I slammed my hand in a car door. 

But no, to answer your question, the worrying isn't like an everyday thing, and it definitely hasn't been going on for months and months. Just when the business stuff gets overwhelming.

I don't know how you eat something like that without getting it all over your clothes. I'd probably have to wear a giant bib, like when you eat lobster. Have you ever had lobster? I tried it once at a wedding, but I think it was overcooked because it was really chewy. The wedding itself was beautiful, though—they got married in this botanical garden, and the hydrangeas were just massive. 

But yeah, the business stuff has definitely been making it hard to keep up with my freelance work and paying bills on time. It's just a lot to juggle right now.

patient.answer:
More days than not? Um, no, I wouldn't say that. It's really just when I have to deal with the shop directly, you know? Like, it hasn't been several months of this constant worrying. It's just recent, since the shop stuff started piling up. 

Actually, speaking of time, I just bought this amazing vintage wall clock for my kitchen. It's one of those retro sunburst ones from the 60s? The spikes are made of this really cool brass that has a nice patina on it. I found it at an estate sale. Estate sales are so wild, you literally just walk through someone's entire life. I found a whole box of old postcards at that same sale, all addressed to this woman named Eleanor in the 1940s. The handwriting was gorgeous—that really swoopy, perfect cursive that nobody learns anymore. I tried to learn calligraphy once, but I am left-handed, so I just ended up smearing the ink everywhere. I had black ink on the side of my hand for like three days. It looked like a terrible bruise. My mom thought I slammed my hand in a car door. 

But no, to answer your question, the worrying isn't like an everyday thing, and it definitely hasn't been going on for months and months. Just when the business stuff gets overwhelming.
